scope: Leviticus 4–7, all 122 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public 4:1–35 and 5:1–19 align directly; public 6:1–7 maps to Hebrew 5:20–26 and public 6:8–30 to Hebrew 6:1–23; chapter 7 aligns directly. Complete original XML records, including numbering notes, are hashed.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains the renewed speech introduction separating these instructions from chapters 1–3.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Unfolds the general heading in natural English without treating unintentional sin as harmless; final words supply its introductory function.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: If someone sins unintentionally in any of the LORD’s commandments concerning things that are not to be done, and does any one of them—
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: When someone sins unintentionally by doing any of the things the LORD’s commandments forbid, these instructions apply.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: If anyone sins unintentionally in any of the LORD’s commandments concerning things that are not to be done, and does any one of them—

verses.rationale: Retains anointed priest, communal consequence, young unblemished bull and repeated sin language; notes purification-offering alternative.
verses.before: if the anointed priest sins so that guilt comes upon the people, then for the sin committed he will bring to the LORD a young bull without defect as a sin offering.
verses.after: If the anointed priest sins and brings guilt on the people, he must bring a young bull without defect to the LORD as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
verses.tsw_comparator: if the anointed priest sins so that guilt comes upon the people, then for the sin committed he shall bring to the LORD a young bull without defect as a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps priest as offerer, hand-laying and slaughter, with before-the-LORD repeated.
verses.before: He will bring the bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter the bull before the LORD.
verses.after: He is to bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall bring the bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before the LORD, lay his hand on the bull’s head, and slaughter the bull before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves anointed designation, partial blood quantity and movement inside.
verses.before: The anointed priest will take some of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: The anointed priest must take some of the bull’s blood into the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: The anointed priest shall take some of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Retains finger, seven applications and curtain-facing location; distinguishes sprinkle from the splashing of chapter 1.
verses.before: The priest will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain of the sanctuary.
verses.after: He is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD, in front of the sanctuary curtain.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain of the sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes inner incense altar from outer altar of burnt offering, horns from base, and applied blood from remainder.
verses.before: The priest will put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and pour all the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: He is to put some blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before the LORD inside the tent of meeting. He must pour all the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the tent’s entrance.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and pour all the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps all-fat scope and two entrail-fat descriptions as the start of a continuing anatomical list.
verses.before: He will remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat around the entrails,
verses.after: He must remove all the fat from the sin-offering bull: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat around the entrails,

verses.rationale: Retains full paired anatomy and the provisional liver-lobe term used in chapter 3 and Exodus 29.
verses.before: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, removed with the kidneys,
verses.after: both kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he is to remove along with the kidneys.
verses.tsw_comparator: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, removed with the kidneys,

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit comparison with peace-offering preparation and altar burning distinct from outside-camp disposal.
verses.before: just as these are removed from the ox of the sacrifice of well-being. The priest will turn them into smoke on the altar of burnt offering.
verses.after: He is to remove these just as they are removed from an ox offered as a peace offering. The priest must burn them on the altar of burnt offering as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: just as these are removed from the ox of the sacrifice of well-being. The priest shall turn them into smoke on the altar of burnt offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves full remaining-carcass inventory and carries the sentence into verse 12.
verses.before: But the bull’s skin, all its flesh, its head, legs, entrails, and dung—
verses.after: But the bull’s skin and all its flesh, its head and legs, its entrails and dung—
verses.tsw_comparator: But the bull’s skin, all its flesh, its head, legs, entrails, and dung—

verses.rationale: Retains whole-bull scope, outside-camp clean place and repeated ash-disposal site, with ordinary burning rather than altar smoke terminology.
verses.before: all the rest of the bull—he will carry outside the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. It will be burned where the ashes are poured out.
verses.after: he must take the whole bull outside the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on a wood fire. It must be burned where the ashes are poured out.
verses.tsw_comparator: all the rest of the bull—he shall carry outside the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. It shall be burned where the ashes are poured out.

verses.rationale: Preserves collective error, lack of awareness and liability, leaving the condition connected to its remedy.
verses.before: If the whole congregation of Israel sins unintentionally and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they do any of the things that the LORD commanded not to be done and become guilty,
verses.after: If the whole Israelite community goes astray without the assembly realizing it, doing something the LORD’s commandments forbid and so becoming guilty,
verses.tsw_comparator: If the whole congregation of Israel sins unintentionally and the matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they do any of the things that the LORD commanded not to be done and become guilty,

verses.rationale: Retains becoming known, corporate offering and young bull, without adding the unblemished qualifier absent here.
verses.before: when the sin they committed becomes known, the assembly will bring a young bull as a sin offering and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: then, when the sin they committed becomes known, the assembly must bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it in front of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: when the sin they committed becomes known, the assembly shall bring a young bull as a sin offering and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Preserves elders’ plural hands and repeated divine presence; uses passive for the unexpressed singular slaughterer rather than assigning him an invented identity.
verses.before: The elders of the congregation will lay their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD, and the bull will be slaughtered before the LORD.
verses.after: The community’s elders are to lay their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD, and the bull is to be slaughtered before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD, and the bull shall be slaughtered before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps named ritual office and interior blood transfer, repeating the earlier priestly case.
verses.before: The anointed priest will bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: The anointed priest is to take some of the bull’s blood into the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: The anointed priest shall bring some of the bull’s blood into the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Retains sevenfold sprinkling and curtain relation without adding sanctuary adjective absent in this verse.
verses.before: The priest will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain.
verses.after: He must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, in front of the curtain.

verses.rationale: Preserves inner/outer altar distinction and blood distribution without importing incense into the first altar’s designation.
verses.before: He will put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and pour all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: He is to put some blood on the horns of the altar before the LORD inside the tent of meeting. He must pour all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the tent’s entrance.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the Tent of Meeting, and pour all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Retains all-fat removal and altar action without repeating an anatomical list not present here.
verses.before: He will remove all its fat and turn it into smoke on the altar.
verses.after: He must remove all the bull’s fat and burn it on the altar as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall remove all its fat and turn it into smoke on the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves emphatic repeated comparison, corporate atonement and forgiveness without adding a formula to the earlier priest’s case.
verses.before: He will do with this bull just as he did with the bull of the sin offering; so he will do with it. The priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
verses.after: He is to do with this bull just as he did with the bull for the sin offering; he must do the same with it. The priest will make atonement for the people, and they will be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall do with this bull just as he did with the bull of the sin offering; so he shall do with it. The priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Retains disposal comparison, outside-camp location and communal offering designation.
verses.before: He will carry the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
verses.after: He must take the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the assembly’s sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall carry the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.

verses.rationale: Keeps leader as male-context office holder, personal his-God relation, unintentional act and guilt.
verses.before: When a leader sins and unintentionally does any one of the things that the LORD his God has commanded not to be done, and becomes guilty,
verses.after: When a leader sins unintentionally by doing something the commandments of the LORD his God forbid, he becomes guilty.
verses.tsw_comparator: When a leader sins and unintentionally does any one of the things that the LORD his God has commanded not to be done, and becomes guilty,

verses.rationale: Reads awareness clause as the next condition for remedy, preserving male goat distinct from common person’s female offering; notes alternative force of or.
verses.before: when the sin he committed is revealed to him, he will bring as his offering a male goat without defect.
verses.after: When the sin he committed is made known to him, he must bring a male goat without defect as his offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: when the sin he committed is made known to him, he shall bring as his offering a male goat without defect.

verses.rationale: Retains leader’s hand and slaughter actions, same location as burnt offering and distinct offering category.
verses.before: He will lay his hand on the goat’s head and slaughter it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.
verses.after: He is to lay his hand on the goat’s head and slaughter it before the LORD where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It is a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall lay his hand on the goat’s head and slaughter it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves finger application, outer altar horns and base, without importing sevenfold inner sprinkling.
verses.before: The priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.
verses.after: The priest is to take some of the sin offering’s blood on his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He must pour its remaining blood at the altar’s base.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

verses.rationale: Retains all-fat comparison, priestly atonement and forgiveness with leader referent clear.
verses.before: He will turn all its fat into smoke on the altar like the fat of the sacrifice of well-being. The priest will make atonement for the leader concerning his sin, and he will be forgiven.
verses.after: He must burn all its fat on the altar as smoke, like the fat of a peace offering. The priest will make atonement for the leader’s sin, and he will be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall turn all its fat into smoke on the altar like the fat of the sacrifice of well-being. The priest shall make atonement for the leader concerning his sin, and he shall be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Keeps individual from the people of the land distinct from priest, assembly and leader, with generic human scope.
verses.before: If any one of the people of the land sins unintentionally by doing any of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done and becomes guilty,
verses.after: If one of the ordinary people sins unintentionally by doing something the LORD’s commandments forbid and so becomes guilty,
verses.tsw_comparator: If any one of the people of the land sins unintentionally by doing any of the things the LORD has commanded not to be done and becomes guilty,

verses.rationale: Retains explicit female animal and awareness transition while using inclusive singular they for the general human case.
verses.before: when the sin committed is revealed, that person will bring as an offering a female goat without defect for the sin committed.
verses.after: then, when the sin becomes known to them, they must bring a female goat without defect as an offering for the sin they committed.
verses.tsw_comparator: when the sin committed is made known, that person shall bring as an offering a female goat without defect for the sin committed.

verses.rationale: Keeps ordinary offerer as hand-laying and slaughtering agent and the repeated offering location.
verses.before: The person will lay a hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering in the place of the burnt offering.
verses.after: They are to lay a hand on the sin offering’s head and slaughter it where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall lay a hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering in the place of the burnt offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves separate priestly role and all-blood remainder, with no inner-sanctuary application added.
verses.before: The priest will take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.
verses.after: The priest must take some of its blood on his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He is to pour all the remaining blood at the altar’s base.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

verses.rationale: Clarifies offerer/priest shift and preserves pleasing aroma unique among these ordinary-person instructions and explicit forgiveness.
verses.before: The priest will remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the sacrifice of well-being, and turn it into smoke on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. The priest will make atonement for the person, and that person will be forgiven.
verses.after: The person bringing the offering is to remove all its fat as the fat is removed from a peace offering. The priest must burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. He will make atonement for that person, and they will be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the sacrifice of well-being, and turn it into smoke on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. The priest shall make atonement for the person, and that person shall be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Keeps sheep alternative and required female sex without narrowing the species to a male lamb.
verses.before: If the person brings a lamb as the offering for a sin offering, it will be a female without defect.
verses.after: If the person brings a sheep as a sin offering, it must be a female without defect.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the person brings a lamb as the offering for a sin offering, it shall be a female without defect.

verses.rationale: Preserves hand/slaughter sequence and repeated sin-offering purpose for the sheep alternative.
verses.before: The person will lay a hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
verses.after: They are to lay a hand on its head and slaughter it as a sin offering where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall lay a hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.

verses.rationale: Keeps outer altar application and all remainder, consistent with the goat case without collapsing repetition.
verses.before: The priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.
verses.after: The priest must take some of the sin offering’s blood on his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He is to pour all the remaining blood at the altar’s base.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves sheep-specific comparison, placement on other offerings, and complete atonement/forgiveness close.
verses.before: The priest will remove all its fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the sacrifice of well-being, and turn it into smoke on the altar upon the offerings by fire to the LORD. The priest will make atonement for the person concerning the sin committed, and that person will be forgiven.
verses.after: The person bringing the sheep must remove all its fat as the fat is removed from a sheep offered as a peace offering. The priest is to burn these parts on the altar, on top of the LORD’s offerings by fire. He will make atonement for the sin that person committed, and they will be forgiven.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall remove all its fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the sacrifice of well-being, and turn it into smoke on the altar upon the offerings by fire to the LORD. The priest shall make atonement for the person concerning the sin committed, and that person shall be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Unfolds oath-bound testimony condition while retaining both seeing and knowing and liability for silence; note preserves curse aspect of oath.
verses.before: If someone sins by hearing a public call to testify and, though a witness who has seen or knows the matter, does not speak, that person will bear guilt.
verses.after: “If someone hears a public call to testify under oath and is a witness—having seen or learned what happened—but does not speak up, they sin and must bear their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone sins by hearing a public call to testify and, though a witness who has seen or knows the matter, does not speak, that person shall bear guilt.

verses.rationale: Keeps three carcass categories, unawareness and both ritual uncleanness and guilt without making all animal touch immoral.
verses.before: Or if someone touches any unclean thing—the carcass of an unclean wild animal, the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean swarming creature—and the matter is hidden from that person, that person is unclean and becomes guilty.
verses.after: Or if someone touches anything unclean—the carcass of an unclean wild animal, livestock, or swarming creature—even without realizing it, they become unclean and guilty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Or if anyone touches any unclean thing—the carcass of an unclean wild animal, the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean swarming creature—and the matter is hidden from that person, that person is unclean and becomes guilty.

verses.rationale: Retains broad human impurity, initial unawareness and subsequent knowledge without inventing the specific contact.
verses.before: Or if someone touches human uncleanness—whatever uncleanness by which a person becomes unclean—and the matter is hidden, when it becomes known that person becomes guilty.
verses.after: Or if someone touches human uncleanness, whatever kind makes a person unclean, without realizing it, then comes to know of it, they are guilty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Or if anyone touches human uncleanness—whatever uncleanness by which a person becomes unclean—and the matter is hidden, when it becomes known that person becomes guilty.

verses.rationale: Preserves harm/good range, repeated rashness, oath and awareness sequence without adding deliberate lying.
verses.before: Or if someone swears rashly with the lips to do evil or to do good—whatever a person may utter rashly in an oath—and the matter is hidden, when it becomes known that person becomes guilty in one of these matters.
verses.after: Or if someone rashly swears to do harm or good—whatever a person might rashly promise under oath—without realizing it, then comes to know of it, they are guilty in one of these matters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Or if anyone swears rashly with the lips to do evil or to do good—whatever a person may utter rashly in an oath—and the matter is hidden, when it becomes known that person becomes guilty in one of these matters.

verses.rationale: Retains explicit confession tied to the particular sin rather than a generic devotional statement.
verses.before: When someone becomes guilty in any one of these, that person will confess the sin committed.
verses.after: When someone is guilty in any of these matters, they must confess the sin they committed.
verses.tsw_comparator: When someone becomes guilty in any one of these, that person shall confess the sin committed.

verses.rationale: Renders asham here as reparation so the stated sin offering is not confused with the distinct ram guilt offering below; keeps female alternatives.
verses.before: The person will bring to the LORD as a guilt offering for the sin committed a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, as a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for the person concerning the sin.
verses.after: As reparation for the sin, they must bring the LORD a female from the flock, a sheep or goat, as a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for their sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall bring to the LORD as a guilt offering for the sin committed a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, as a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for the person concerning the sin.

verses.rationale: Retains economic alternative, exact two birds, two species choices and different offering roles for each bird.
verses.before: If the person cannot afford a sheep, then as the guilt offering for the sin committed that person will bring to the LORD two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
verses.after: If they cannot afford a sheep or goat, they must bring the LORD two turtledoves or two young pigeons as reparation for their sin: one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the person cannot afford a sheep, then as the guilt offering for the sin committed that person shall bring to the LORD two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps sin offering first and neck action without complete separation, distinct from chapter 1’s bird burnt offering.
verses.before: The person will bring them to the priest, who will first present the one for the sin offering. The priest will pinch off its head at the neck without severing it completely.
verses.after: They are to bring the birds to the priest, who must first present the one for the sin offering. He is to wring its head at the back of the neck without severing it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall bring them to the priest, who shall first present the one for the sin offering. The priest shall pinch off its head at the neck without severing it completely.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes sprinkling from draining and side from base; retains offering category.
verses.before: The priest will sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering against the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood will be drained at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
verses.after: He must sprinkle some of its blood against the side of the altar and drain the rest at the altar’s base. It is a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering against the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps second bird’s distinct category, prescribed procedure and repeated forgiveness.
verses.before: The priest will offer the second as a burnt offering according to the ordinance. The priest will make atonement for the person concerning the sin committed, and that person will be forgiven.
verses.after: He is to prepare the second bird as a burnt offering according to the rule. The priest will make atonement for the sin the person committed, and they will be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall offer the second as a burnt offering according to the ordinance. The priest shall make atonement for the person concerning the sin committed, and that person shall be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Preserves second economic accommodation, exact tenth-ephah and both prohibited additions, contrasting chapter 2.
verses.before: If the person cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then as an offering for the sin committed that person will bring one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. No oil will be put on it and no frankincense placed on it, for it is a sin offering.
verses.after: If they cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, they must bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering for their sin. They must not put oil or frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the person cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then as an offering for the sin committed that person shall bring one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. No oil shall be put on it and no frankincense placed on it, for it is a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Keeps priest’s handful, memorial function, placement on offerings and repeated category despite grain material.
verses.before: The person will bring it to the priest, and the priest will take from it a handful as its memorial portion and turn it into smoke on the altar, upon the offerings by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
verses.after: They are to bring it to the priest. He must take a handful as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar, on top of the LORD’s offerings by fire. It is a sin offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take from it a handful as its memorial portion and turn it into smoke on the altar, upon the offerings by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves forgiveness and priestly remainder comparison while not relabeling the flour sin offering as a grain offering.
verses.before: The priest will make atonement for the person concerning the sin committed in any of these matters, and that person will be forgiven. The remainder will belong to the priest, as with the grain offering.”
verses.after: The priest will make atonement for the sin the person committed in any of these matters, and they will be forgiven. The remainder will belong to the priest, as with a grain offering.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall make atonement for the person concerning the sin committed in any of these matters, and that person shall be forgiven. The remainder shall belong to the priest, as with the grain offering.”

verses.rationale: Retains new speech formula before instructions on holy property.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps breach of trust, unintentional holy-property offense, unblemished ram and second-person valuation in sanctuary shekels without inventing a sum.
verses.before: “If someone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally in regard to the LORD’s holy things, that person will bring to the LORD as a guilt offering a ram without defect from the flock, valued in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, as a guilt offering.
verses.after: “When someone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally in regard to the LORD’s holy things, they must bring the LORD a ram without defect from the flock as a guilt offering, valued according to your assessment in silver shekels by the sanctuary standard.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If anyone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally in regard to the LORD’s holy things, that person shall bring to the LORD as a guilt offering a ram without defect from the flock, valued in silver shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, as a guilt offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves restitution plus fifth and priest recipient, distinct from sacrificial ram; the holy-property loss remains concrete.
verses.before: The person will make restitution for the holy thing in which wrong was done, add one-fifth to it, and give it to the priest. The priest will make atonement with the ram of the guilt offering, and that person will be forgiven.
verses.after: They must make restitution for the loss involving the holy things, add a fifth of its value, and give it to the priest. The priest will make atonement for them with the ram of the guilt offering, and they will be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall make restitution for the holy thing in which wrong was done, add one-fifth to it, and give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement with the ram of the guilt offering, and that person shall be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Retains liability despite ignorance and repeated guilt-bearing claim without adding deliberate intent.
verses.before: If someone sins by doing any of the things that the LORD has commanded not to be done, though the person did not know it, that person is guilty and will bear guilt.
verses.after: If someone sins by doing anything the LORD’s commandments forbid, even without knowing it, they are guilty and must bear their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone sins by doing any of the things that the LORD has commanded not to be done, though the person did not know it, that person is guilty and shall bear guilt.

verses.rationale: Keeps assessed ram, priest transfer, repeated unintentional/unaware language and forgiveness.
verses.before: The person will bring to the priest a ram without defect from the flock, according to the valuation, as a guilt offering. The priest will make atonement for the person concerning the unintentional wrong committed without knowing it, and that person will be forgiven.
verses.after: They must bring the priest a ram without defect from the flock, at your assessed value, as a guilt offering. The priest will make atonement for the error they committed unintentionally and without knowing it, and they will be forgiven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The person shall bring to the priest a ram without defect from the flock, according to the valuation, as a guilt offering. The priest shall make atonement for the person concerning the unintentional wrong committed without knowing it, and that person shall be forgiven.

verses.rationale: Preserves asham wordplay and emphatic guilt without collapsing offering and liability into one referent.
verses.before: It is a guilt offering; that person has certainly become guilty before the LORD.
verses.after: It is a guilt offering; they have indeed incurred guilt before the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: It is a guilt offering; that person has certainly become guilty before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains speech formula at public chapter start, bound to complete Hebrew 5:20 including numbering note.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves offense against God enacted through neighbor wrong, all four property categories and open conditional syntax.
verses.before: “If someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving a neighbor concerning something entrusted for safekeeping, or a pledge, or something taken by robbery, or by oppressing a neighbor,
verses.after: “When someone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving a neighbor about a deposit or something entrusted to them, by robbery, or by defrauding that neighbor,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If anyone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving a neighbor concerning something entrusted for safekeeping, or a pledge, or something taken by robbery, or by oppressing a neighbor,

verses.rationale: Keeps lost property, denial and false oath with broad summary, continuing the condition across labels.
verses.before: or by finding something lost and lying about it, swearing falsely in any of these things by which a person may sin,
verses.after: or by finding lost property, lying about it, and swearing falsely—in any of these ways that people sin—
verses.tsw_comparator: or by finding something lost and lying about it, swearing falsely in any of these things by which a person may sin,

verses.rationale: Retains full repeated restitution inventory and guilt transition, with no deleted property category.
verses.before: then, when that person has sinned and becomes guilty, the person will restore what was taken by robbery, what was obtained by oppression, what was entrusted for safekeeping, or the lost thing that was found,
verses.after: when they sin and become guilty, they must return what they stole or obtained by fraud, the deposit entrusted to them, or the lost property they found,
verses.tsw_comparator: then, when that person has sinned and becomes guilty, the person shall restore what was taken by robbery, what was obtained by oppression, what was entrusted for safekeeping, or the lost thing that was found,

verses.rationale: Keeps principal plus fifth and direct repayment to owner, with disputed day-of-asham phrase noted rather than forced into one ceremony.
verses.before: or anything about which the person swore falsely. The person will restore it in full and add one-fifth to it, giving it to its owner on the day the person is found guilty.
verses.after: or anything about which they swore falsely. They must repay its full value, add a fifth, and give it to its owner on the day they make reparation.
verses.tsw_comparator: or anything about which the person swore falsely. The person shall restore it in full and add one-fifth to it, giving it to its owner on the day the person is found guilty.

verses.rationale: Retains divine recipient, ram qualification, second-person valuation and priest as recipient of the animal.
verses.before: Then the person will bring to the LORD as a guilt offering a ram without defect from the flock, according to the valuation, and bring it to the priest.
verses.after: They must bring the LORD their guilt offering: a ram without defect from the flock, at your assessed value, brought to the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the person shall bring to the LORD as a guilt offering a ram without defect from the flock, according to the valuation, and bring it to the priest.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine presence, priestly atonement and all-listed-offenses forgiveness as connected conclusion.
verses.before: The priest will make atonement for the person before the LORD, and that person will be forgiven for whatever was done to become guilty.”
verses.after: The priest will make atonement for them before the LORD, and they will be forgiven for any of these things they did that made them guilty.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall make atonement for the person before the LORD, and that person shall be forgiven for whatever was done to become guilty.”

verses.rationale: Retains fresh speech opening at Hebrew chapter 6:1 while keeping public label 6:8.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves named priestly recipients, overnight duration, hearth and first continuous-fire requirement.
verses.before: “Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering will remain on the hearth upon the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar will be kept burning on it.
verses.after: “Command Aaron and his sons: This is the instruction for the burnt offering. It must remain on the altar’s hearth all night until morning, and the altar fire must be kept burning.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering shall remain on the hearth upon the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.

verses.rationale: Keeps both linen garments, body contact and ash removal/location without euphemizing bodily requirement.
verses.before: The priest will put on his linen garment and put linen undergarments on his body. He will remove the ashes to which the fire has reduced the burnt offering on the altar and place them beside the altar.
verses.after: The priest must put on his linen garment, with linen undergarments against his body. He is to remove the ashes left when the fire consumes the burnt offering on the altar and place them beside the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall put on his linen garment and put linen undergarments on his body. He shall remove the ashes to which the fire has reduced the burnt offering on the altar and place them beside the altar.

verses.rationale: Retains clothing change before transport and clean place outside camp, distinct from altar-side staging.
verses.before: Then he will take off those garments, put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
verses.after: Then he must take off those garments, put on other clothes, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he shall take off those garments, put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated fire prohibition, daily cadence and burnt/peace offering roles in ordered routine.
verses.before: The fire on the altar will be kept burning; it will not go out. The priest will burn wood on it every morning, arrange the burnt offering on it, and turn the fat of the sacrifices of well-being into smoke on it.
verses.after: The fire on the altar must be kept burning; it must not go out. Morning after morning, the priest must add wood, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat of the peace offerings on it as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fire on the altar shall be kept burning; it shall not go out. The priest shall burn wood on it every morning, arrange the burnt offering on it, and turn the fat of the sacrifices of well-being into smoke on it.

verses.rationale: Retains full repeated prohibition instead of treating repetition as redundancy.
verses.before: Fire will be kept burning on the altar continually; it will not go out.
verses.after: Fire must burn continually on the altar; it must not go out.
verses.tsw_comparator: Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.

verses.rationale: Keeps separate offering heading, named sons and double divine/altar orientation.
verses.before: This is the law of the grain offering. Aaron’s sons will present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.
verses.after: This is the instruction for the grain offering. Aaron’s sons are to present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law of the grain offering. Aaron’s sons shall present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves handful versus all-incense quantities, memorial function and aroma language.
verses.before: One of them will take from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, some of its oil, and all the frankincense that is on the grain offering, and turn its memorial portion into smoke on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: The priest must take a handful of the grain offering’s fine flour and oil, together with all its frankincense, and burn it on the altar as its memorial portion, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: One of them shall take from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, some of its oil, and all the frankincense that is on the grain offering, and turn its memorial portion into smoke on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains named eaters, unleavened state, holy-place requirement and repeated eating at specified courtyard.
verses.before: Aaron and his sons will eat what remains. It will be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they will eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: Aaron and his sons are to eat what remains. It must be eaten without leaven in a holy place; they are to eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they shall eat it in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct divine first person, priestly share and three offering categories under superlative holiness.
verses.before: It will not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their portion from my offerings by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
verses.after: It must not be baked with leaven. I have given it to them as their share of my offerings by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their portion from my offerings by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves specifically male priestly line, lasting generation scope and holiness-by-contact wording with alternative prerequisite reading noted.
verses.before: Every male among Aaron’s descendants may eat it. This will be a perpetual portion throughout your generations from the offerings by fire to the LORD. Whatever touches them will become holy.”
verses.after: Every male among Aaron’s descendants may eat it as a lasting share of the LORD’s offerings by fire throughout your generations. Whatever touches them becomes holy.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Every male among Aaron’s descendants may eat it. This shall be a perpetual portion throughout your generations from the offerings by fire to the LORD. Whatever touches them shall become holy.”

verses.rationale: Keeps new divine speech before anointed priest’s grain provision.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Retains plural Aaron/sons with singular anointing, day and regularity tension, exact tenth-ephah and equal halves.
verses.before: “This is the offering that Aaron and his sons will bring to the LORD on the day one of them is anointed: one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
verses.after: “This is the offering Aaron and his sons are to present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This is the offering that Aaron and his sons shall bring to the LORD on the day one of them is anointed: one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.

verses.rationale: Preserves griddle, oil, preparation and pieces while noting uncertain rare cooking terms without inventing a precise recipe.
verses.before: It will be prepared with oil on a griddle. When it is well mixed, you will bring it. You will present it in baked pieces as a grain offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.after: It must be prepared with oil on a griddle. Bring it well mixed, presenting the grain offering in baked pieces as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: It shall be prepared with oil on a griddle. When it is well mixed, you shall bring it. You shall present it in baked pieces as a grain offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps successor within sons, anointing and whole consumption distinct from priests’ edible grain share.
verses.before: The priest from among Aaron’s sons who is anointed in his place will prepare it. It is a perpetual statute: it will be entirely turned into smoke for the LORD.
verses.after: The priest anointed to succeed him from among his sons must prepare it. As a lasting requirement for the LORD, it must be burned entirely as smoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest from among Aaron’s sons who is anointed in his place shall prepare it. It is a perpetual statute: it shall be entirely turned into smoke for the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains comprehensive priest-offering scope and explicit no-eating contrast with ordinary offerings.
verses.before: Every grain offering of a priest will be wholly burned; it will not be eaten.”
verses.after: Every grain offering made by a priest must be burned entirely; it must not be eaten.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Every grain offering of a priest shall be wholly burned; it shall not be eaten.”

verses.rationale: Preserves speech boundary before priestly sin-offering instruction.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps priestly audience, slaughter-place correspondence and superlative holiness.
verses.before: “Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering will be slaughtered before the LORD. It is most holy.
verses.after: “Tell Aaron and his sons: This is the instruction for the sin offering. It must be slaughtered before the LORD where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It is most holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before the LORD. It is most holy.

verses.rationale: Retains officiating priest’s portion and explicit eating location, without broadening access.
verses.before: The priest who offers it for sin will eat it. It will be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.
verses.after: The priest who presents it as a sin offering is to eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

verses.rationale: Keeps contact holiness, accidental blood stain and holy washing location; notes alternate holiness prerequisite interpretation.
verses.before: Whatever touches its flesh will become holy. If any of its blood is splashed on a garment, you will wash the part splashed with blood in a holy place.
verses.after: Whatever touches its flesh becomes holy. If any of its blood splashes onto a garment, you must wash the stained area in a holy place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Whatever touches its flesh shall become holy. If any of its blood is splashed on a garment, you shall wash the part splashed with blood in a holy place.

verses.rationale: Preserves different treatments for porous pottery and bronze without adding a hygienic explanation as source meaning.
verses.before: An earthen vessel in which it is boiled will be broken, but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, that vessel will be scoured and rinsed with water.
verses.after: An earthenware vessel used to boil it must be broken. If it was boiled in a bronze vessel, that vessel must be scoured and rinsed with water.
verses.tsw_comparator: An earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken, but if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, that vessel shall be scoured and rinsed with water.

verses.rationale: Keeps specifically male priestly eaters and repeated holiness designation.
verses.before: Every male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
verses.after: Every male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.

verses.rationale: Preserves exception for interior-blood offerings and disposal, connecting chapter 4 without making all sin offerings edible.
verses.before: But no sin offering will be eaten if any of its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place. It will be burned with fire.
verses.after: But no sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the sanctuary may be eaten. It must be burned with fire.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But no sin offering shall be eaten if any of its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place. It shall be burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Retains distinct category and superlative holiness, with continuing divine speech across editorial chapter boundary.
verses.before: “This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.
verses.after: “This is the instruction for the guilt offering. It is most holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps unspecified plural slaughterers unassigned and identifies understood priestly blood agent, using splash distinct from sprinkle.
verses.before: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the guilt offering will be slaughtered, and its blood will be dashed against all sides of the altar.
verses.after: The guilt offering is to be slaughtered where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and the priest must splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the guilt offering shall be slaughtered, and its blood shall be dashed against all sides of the altar.

verses.rationale: Preserves all-fat scope, tail and covering, with anatomical list continuing across label.
verses.before: All its fat will be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails,
verses.after: All its fat must be presented: the fat tail and the fat covering the entrails,
verses.tsw_comparator: All its fat shall be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails,

verses.rationale: Retains full repeated anatomy and provisional liver-lobe interpretation consistent across offerings.
verses.before: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, removed with the kidneys.
verses.after: both kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which is to be removed along with the kidneys.
verses.tsw_comparator: the two kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the appendage of the liver, removed with the kidneys.

verses.rationale: Keeps officiating priest, altar action and repeated offering category without adding pleasing-aroma formula absent here.
verses.before: The priest will turn them into smoke on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
verses.after: The priest is to burn these on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall turn them into smoke on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves male priestly scope, location and holiness as three clear claims.
verses.before: Every male among the priests may eat it. It will be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
verses.after: Every male among the priests may eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every male among the priests may eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared ownership rule while not collapsing distinct offering categories or interior-blood exception.
verses.before: The law is the same for the sin offering and the guilt offering: the priest who makes atonement with it will have it.
verses.after: The same instruction applies to the sin offering and the guilt offering: the offering belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The law is the same for the sin offering and the guilt offering: the priest who makes atonement with it shall have it.

verses.rationale: Retains priestly skin allocation without suggesting the rest of a burnt offering becomes food.
verses.before: The priest who presents anyone’s burnt offering will have for himself the skin of the burnt offering he has presented.
verses.after: When a priest presents someone’s burnt offering, the skin of that offering belongs to that priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest who presents anyone’s burnt offering shall have for himself the skin of the burnt offering he has presented.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three cooking methods and officiating priest’s ownership, corresponding to chapter 2.
verses.before: Every grain offering baked in an oven, and every offering prepared in a pan or on a griddle, will belong to the priest who presents it.
verses.after: Every grain offering baked in an oven, prepared in a pan, or cooked on a griddle belongs to the priest who presents it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every grain offering baked in an oven, and every offering prepared in a pan or on a griddle, shall belong to the priest who presents it.

verses.rationale: Preserves oil/dry alternatives and equal sharing among sons, without silently harmonizing it with the individual share in verse 9.
verses.before: Every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, will belong equally to all the sons of Aaron.
verses.after: Every grain offering mixed with oil or left dry belongs equally to all Aaron’s sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, shall belong equally to all the sons of Aaron.

verses.rationale: Retains new category heading and divine recipient, keeping peace-offering terminology from Exodus and chapter 3.
verses.before: This is the law of the sacrifice of well-being that a person may offer to the LORD.
verses.after: This is the instruction for a peace offering presented to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law of the sacrifice of well-being that a person may offer to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves thanksgiving motive and all three unleavened preparation descriptions with distinct oil treatments; rare mixed term noted.
verses.before: If it is offered for thanksgiving, then together with the thanksgiving sacrifice the person will offer unleavened cakes mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and cakes of fine flour well mixed with oil.
verses.after: If it is presented in thanksgiving, the person bringing it must bring with the thanksgiving sacrifice unleavened cakes mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and cakes of fine flour well mixed with oil.
verses.tsw_comparator: If it is offered for thanksgiving, then together with the thanksgiving sacrifice the person shall offer unleavened cakes mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and cakes of fine flour well mixed with oil.

verses.rationale: Retains additional leavened bread rather than mechanically importing chapter 2’s altar prohibition to all gifts.
verses.before: Together with the sacrifice of well-being for thanksgiving, the person will bring the offering with cakes of leavened bread.
verses.after: Along with these, they must bring loaves of leavened bread with the thanksgiving sacrifice of their peace offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Together with the sacrifice of well-being for thanksgiving, the person shall bring the offering with cakes of leavened bread.

verses.rationale: Keeps one per kind, contribution terminology and particular priest identified by blood handling.
verses.before: From each kind of offering one portion will be presented as a contribution to the LORD. It will belong to the priest who dashes the blood of the sacrifice of well-being.
verses.after: They are to present one of each kind as a contribution to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who splashes the peace offering’s blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: From each kind of offering one portion shall be presented as a contribution to the LORD. It shall belong to the priest who dashes the blood of the sacrifice of well-being.

verses.rationale: Preserves same-day eating and explicit overnight prohibition, distinct from vow/freewill allowance.
verses.before: The flesh of the sacrifice of well-being for thanksgiving will be eaten on the day it is offered; none of it will be left until morning.
verses.after: The meat of the thanksgiving peace offering must be eaten on the day it is offered. None of it may be left until morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: The flesh of the sacrifice of well-being for thanksgiving shall be eaten on the day it is offered; none of it shall be left until morning.

verses.rationale: Keeps two alternative motives and two-day consumption window.
verses.before: If the sacrifice is for a vow or a freewill offering, it will be eaten on the day the sacrifice is offered, and what remains may be eaten on the next day.
verses.after: If the sacrifice is a vow offering or a freewill offering, it is to be eaten on the day it is offered, and whatever remains may also be eaten the next day.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the sacrifice is for a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day the sacrifice is offered, and what remains may be eaten on the next day.

verses.rationale: Retains third-day disposal and ordinary burning rather than renewed altar presentation.
verses.before: But what remains of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day will be burned with fire.
verses.after: Any meat from the sacrifice still left on the third day must be burned with fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: But what remains of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves acceptance/credit distinctions, defiled status and eater liability without resolving the rule into a later intent-based interpretation.
verses.before: If any of the flesh of the sacrifice of well-being is eaten on the third day, the one who offered it will not be accepted, and it will not be credited to that person. It is a repulsive thing, and the person who eats it will bear guilt.
verses.after: If any meat from the peace offering is eaten on the third day, the offering will not be accepted or credited to the person who brought it. It becomes a defiled thing, and anyone who eats it must bear their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: If any of the flesh of the sacrifice of well-being is eaten on the third day, the one who offered it will not be accepted, and it will not be credited to that person. It is a repulsive thing, and the person who eats it shall bear guilt.

verses.rationale: Keeps contact-based meat restriction and clean eater permission, with other supplied to clarify contrast.
verses.before: Flesh that touches anything unclean will not be eaten; it will be burned with fire. As for other flesh, everyone who is clean may eat it.
verses.after: Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it must be burned with fire. As for other meat, anyone who is clean may eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flesh that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. As for other flesh, everyone who is clean may eat it.

verses.rationale: Preserves uncleanness condition, divine ownership and cut-off sanction without defining its mechanism as mere exclusion.
verses.before: But a person who eats flesh from the LORD’s sacrifice of well-being while uncleanness is upon that person will be cut off from the people.
verses.after: But anyone who is unclean and eats meat from a peace offering belonging to the LORD will be cut off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: But a person who eats flesh from the LORD’s sacrifice of well-being while uncleanness is upon that person shall be cut off from the people.

verses.rationale: Retains all three impurity categories and compound condition before repeated sanction.
verses.before: If someone touches anything unclean—human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean swarming thing—and then eats from the flesh of the LORD’s sacrifice of well-being, that person will be cut off from the people.”
verses.after: Anyone who touches something unclean—human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean detestable thing—and then eats meat from a peace offering belonging to the LORD will be cut off from their people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone touches anything unclean—human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean swarming thing—and then eats from the flesh of the LORD’s sacrifice of well-being, that person shall be cut off from the people.”

verses.rationale: Keeps speech formula separating fat and blood instruction.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves all three animal kinds and comprehensive fat prohibition within that named scope.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: You will not eat any fat of an ox, sheep, or goat.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: You must not eat any fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: You shall not eat any fat of an ox, sheep, or goat.

verses.rationale: Keeps carcass/torn-animal alternatives, permission for nonfood uses and emphatic eating ban.
verses.before: The fat of an animal that dies by itself or is torn by wild animals may be used for any other purpose, but you will not eat it.
verses.after: Fat from an animal that dies on its own or is torn by wild animals may be used for other work, but you must never eat it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The fat of an animal that dies by itself or is torn by wild animals may be used for any other purpose, but you shall not eat it.

verses.rationale: Preserves sacrificial-kind scope and cut-off consequence without restricting only to fat already on the altar.
verses.before: For anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which an offering by fire is presented to the LORD, the person who eats it will be cut off from the people.
verses.after: Anyone who eats fat from an animal of the kind presented as an offering by fire to the LORD will be cut off from their people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which an offering by fire is presented to the LORD, the person who eats it shall be cut off from the people.

verses.rationale: Keeps all-dwellings scope and both bird and land-animal blood, not reducing to mammal sacrifices.
verses.before: You will not eat any blood, whether of bird or animal, in any of your dwellings.
verses.after: Wherever you live, you must not eat any blood, whether from birds or livestock.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not eat any blood, whether of bird or animal, in any of your dwellings.

verses.rationale: Retains full emphatic blood prohibition and repeated sanction as independent closure.
verses.before: Any person who eats any blood will be cut off from the people.”
verses.after: Anyone who eats any blood will be cut off from their people.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Any person who eats any blood shall be cut off from the people.”

verses.rationale: Preserves renewed speech introduction before contribution shares.
verses.before: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.after: The LORD spoke to Moses:
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

verses.rationale: Preserves distinction between whole peace offering and the gift brought from it, with divine recipient repeated.
verses.before: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: The one who brings a sacrifice of well-being to the LORD will bring from that sacrifice the portion presented to the LORD.
verses.after: “Tell the Israelites: Anyone bringing a peace offering to the LORD must bring the LORD a gift from that sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Speak to the Israelites, saying: The one who brings a sacrifice of well-being to the LORD shall bring from that sacrifice the portion presented to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains personal hands, fat/breast distinction and presentation rite, using the wave-offering terminology of Exodus 29 with uncertain motion noted.
verses.before: With the person’s own hands the offerings by fire to the LORD will be brought. The fat will be brought with the breast, so that the breast may be elevated as an elevation offering before the LORD.
verses.after: With their own hands they are to bring the LORD’s offerings by fire: the fat together with the breast, bringing the breast to be waved as a wave offering before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: With the person’s own hands the offerings by fire to the LORD shall be brought. The fat shall be brought with the breast, so that the breast may be elevated as an elevation offering before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps burned fat distinct from shared priestly breast and named recipients.
verses.before: The priest will turn the fat into smoke on the altar, but the breast will belong to Aaron and his sons.
verses.after: The priest must burn the fat on the altar as smoke, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: The priest shall turn the fat into smoke on the altar, but the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.

verses.rationale: Retains right side, thigh anatomy and contribution term distinct from the breast’s wave offering.
verses.before: You will give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your sacrifices of well-being.
verses.after: From your peace offerings, give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your sacrifices of well-being.

verses.rationale: Preserves officiating son’s specific portion, distinguished from breast shared among sons.
verses.before: The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the sacrifice of well-being will have the right thigh as his portion.
verses.after: The son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat of the peace offering is to receive the right thigh as his share.
verses.tsw_comparator: The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the sacrifice of well-being shall have the right thigh as his portion.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine first-person assignment, distinct presentation terms, named priestly family and repeated Israelite source.
verses.before: For I have taken from the Israelites the breast of the elevation offering and the thigh of the contribution from their sacrifices of well-being, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as a perpetual portion from the Israelites.”
verses.after: For I have taken the breast of the wave offering and the contributed thigh from the Israelites’ peace offerings and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a lasting share from the Israelites.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have taken from the Israelites the breast of the elevation offering and the thigh of the contribution from their sacrifices of well-being, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as a perpetual portion from the Israelites.”

verses.rationale: Reads mishhah as allotted share connected with anointing, preserving priestly installation occasion and divine service.
verses.before: This is the allotted portion of Aaron and the allotted portion of his sons from the offerings by fire to the LORD, from the day they were brought near to serve the LORD as priests.
verses.after: This is the share assigned to Aaron and his sons from the LORD’s offerings by fire, from the day they were brought forward to serve the LORD as priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the allotted portion of Aaron and the allotted portion of his sons from the offerings by fire to the LORD, from the day they were brought near to serve the LORD as priests.

verses.rationale: Retains command, Israelite donors, anointing day and enduring generation scope without naming unexpressed anointer.
verses.before: The LORD commanded that this be given to them from the Israelites on the day they were anointed. It is a perpetual statute throughout their generations.
verses.after: The LORD commanded the Israelites to give them this on the day they were anointed, as a lasting statute throughout their generations.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD commanded that this be given to them from the Israelites on the day they were anointed. It is a perpetual statute throughout their generations.

verses.rationale: Keeps all six categories in order and carries summary into source-location clause of verse 38.
verses.before: This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the sacrifice of well-being,
verses.after: These are the instructions for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offerings, and the peace offering,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the sacrifice of well-being,

verses.rationale: Retains Moses, mountain and wilderness both named, command occasion and repeated divine recipient closing the unit.
verses.before: which the LORD commanded Moses at Mount Sinai on the day the LORD commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.after: which the LORD gave Moses on Mount Sinai when he commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
verses.tsw_comparator: which the LORD commanded Moses at Mount Sinai on the day the LORD commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
